title: AppreciateYa – Workplace Gratitude App
description: A small workplace gratitude app for sending kudos, virtual coffees, and gift cards to teammates.

body.raw:
![AppreciateYa Home Page](/img/appreciate/appreciateYa.jpg)
![AI Kudos Generator](/img/appreciate/AI.png)

> AppreciateYa is a simple way to send a teammate a thank-you, a virtual coffee, or a small gift. I made it for the everyday wins that are easy to overlook when a team works remotely.

---

## 💻 Try the App

- 👉 [Launch AppreciateYa](https://appreciate-ya.vercel.app/)
- 💾 [View Code on GitHub](https://github.com/applescan/appreciate.ya)

---

## 🌟 Key Features

- 💌 **Send Personalized Kudos** – Celebrate teammates with gratitude messages, coffee, or gift cards.
- 🏆 **Track Top MVPs** – Discover who gives and receives the most appreciation.
- 📊 **See Culture Insights** – Get a visual pulse on your team’s appreciation habits.
- 🤖 **AI Suggestions** – Let AI help you write heartfelt notes with just one click!

---

## ✨ Why This Matters

When work gets busy, a quick thank-you can be the first thing to disappear. This was my attempt to make that small gesture easier.

---

## 🧠 New Feature: AI Kudos Writer

Not sure how to word it? The built-in **AI Kudos Generator** offers a starting point you can make your own.

---

## 🛠 Built With

- T3 Stack
- Next.js
- Prisma
- Tailwind CSS
- GraphQL
- Supabase
- React
- TypeScript
- Node.js
- Canva & Figma

title: [Google Play] Diamond Valley 2024 (KR,TW,JP)
description: A Google Play campaign with a mini-game and regional features for Korea, Taiwan, and Japan.

body.raw:
![Diamond Valley Japan](/img/diamond-valley/diamond-valley.webp)
![Diamond Valley Pages](/img/diamond-valley/diamond-valley-2.webp)

> Diamond Valley returned in 2024 with a new mini-game, updated artwork, and different features for Korea, Taiwan, and Japan. The campaign gave players plenty of reasons to come back, compete, and share.

---

## 🎥 Campaign Showreel

- 💻 [View Reel on Youtube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EhgduXxqRgM&list=TLGGvUWUXUw3ikEwOTA3MjAyNQ&t=4s)

---

## 🌟 Key Features

- 🎯 **Diamond Hero Mini-Game** – New gameplay mode with leaderboard-driven competition and over 1.4 million plays.
- 🎨 **Remastered Graphics** – Updated character designs by Muchang increase appeal and user engagement.
- 🤝 **Community & Multiplayer** – Taiwan’s team challenges, group emojis, and leaderboards boost collaboration and friendly rivalry.
- 📱 **Circle to Search** – Japan’s unique interactive quest system, leveraging Android’s Circle to Search feature for immersive gameplay.
- 🎁 **Sweepstakes System** – Flexible auto/manual entry options with gamified UI, resulting in 3.7 million entries and 172,000+ registrations.

---

## 🛠 My Role

I was one of the front-end developers on the website, working on the homepage and sweepstakes pages. For the Japan version, I built the gacha pop-up.

---

## ✨ Evolution & Impact

The original Korean campaign from 2023 grew into versions for Taiwan and Japan, each with its own features. Role-play mechanics, quests, and team rewards helped lift registrations 2.7× across the campaign.

---

## 🛠 Built With

- Angular 19
- Pixi.js
- TypeScript
- CSS3
- HTML5
- Node.js
- Google Play API integrations

---

## 🎥 Campaign Showreel

## 🤝 Collaboration & Sponsorships

Partnerships with Muchang, Google, and sponsors like Honkai: Star Rail, Solo Leveling, Genshin Impact, and Le Sserafim brought exciting brand integrations into the gameplay, elevating the experience for players and fans alike.

---

> Diamond Valley 2024 demonstrates how creative regional adaptations and gamified experiences can drive meaningful engagement in diverse markets.

title: Hikitia Air – Airline Booking UI & UX Case Study
description: A UX Design Institute case study on making an airline booking flow clearer and easier to use.

body.raw:
![Banner 1](/img/hikitia/banner1.jpg)
![Banner 2](/img/hikitia/banner2.jpg)
![Banner 3](/img/hikitia/banner3.jpg)

> ✈️ Hikitia Air was a fictional airline project I completed while studying at the UX Design Institute. I researched how people book flights, tested existing sites, and turned what I learned into a prototype with a clearer booking flow.

---

## 🔍 Competitive Benchmark

Before jumping into design, I studied top airline booking platforms to understand what they’re doing right (or wrong). Key questions I explored:

- What UX patterns are working well and worth adopting?
- What pain points keep recurring across platforms?
- What standards should I incorporate into my own flow?

![Competitive Benchmark](/img/hikitia/competitiveBenchmark.jpg)

👉 [Download the full research](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1O41oy2mXxg4WHdttVp4EIWDrc8L7RDEu/view?usp=sharing)

---

## 🧪 Usability Testing

I ran usability tests on real airline websites to capture user behaviors, habits, and frustrations. A few takeaways:

- Users browse flights on mobile but prefer booking on desktop.
- Incomplete or scattered info causes user hesitation.
- Fare breakdowns were often unclear or misleading.

![Usability Testing](/img/hikitia/usabilityTesting.jpg)

---

## 🧠 Affinity Diagram

Once research was gathered, I organized insights into themes using an affinity diagram. This helped synthesize findings and identify clear priorities for design.

- Observations from benchmarks, surveys, and tests were written on sticky notes.
- Grouped into thematic clusters in Miro.
- These categories informed both the Customer Journey and User Flow.

![Affinity Diagram](/img/hikitia/affinityDiagram.jpg)

👉 [Download the affinity diagram](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bxbu8jYEQaOKrNkOtWUaDKARAWF5SweO/view?usp=sharing)

---

## 🧭 Customer Journey Map

I mapped the booking journey from start to finish so I could see where people got stuck or needed more information.

![Customer Journey](/img/hikitia/customerJourney.jpg)

---

## 🧩 User Flow

The user flow mapped out the ideal booking process and ensured every UX decision was based on real user insights.

- Covers the high-level steps in booking a flight
- Solves pain points identified in the journey map
- Prepares the foundation for wireframes and prototypes

![User Flow](/img/hikitia/userFlow.jpg)

👉 [Download the user flow](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hWYWnPCmVyw9EZXdwIdv7S0LjrWvxfky/view?usp=sharing)

---

## ✨ High-Fidelity Prototype (Annotated)

I used the research to design a high-fidelity Figma prototype that keeps the important information and choices clear.

![Prototype 1](/img/hikitia/anno1.jpg)
![Prototype 2](/img/hikitia/anno2.jpg)

👉 [Download the prototype](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1WQujyCpGtKgX9nqwViM1nZnIBNMxWmZu/view?usp=sharing)

---

## 🧪 Try the Prototype

👉 [View Interactive Prototype on Figma](https://www.figma.com/proto/kYbZQzyFiQLNmRcuyHwCK0/FeliciaFelicia_Project11?type=design&t=8QoeQDWaLhHxv6pM-1&scaling=scale-down&page-id=0%3A1&node-id=120-117&starting-point-node-id=120%3A117)

---

## 🎯 Results

This project took me from early research through to an interactive prototype. More than anything, it taught me to ask better questions before jumping into a solution.

title: Mi Casa - Virtual House Tour
description: A virtual tour of my home with small interactions, eight mini-games, and leaderboards.

body.raw:
![Mi Casa living room exploration scene](/img/mi-casa/1.png)
![Mi Casa dialogue and room interactions](/img/mi-casa/2.png)

> Mi Casa is a small playable version of my home. You can wander through the rooms, find little details about me, and stumble into mini-games along the way. I wanted to make something more personal than a standard portfolio page.

---

## 🎮 Try the Game

- 👉 [Play Mi Casa](https://mi-casa-xi.vercel.app/)
- 💻 [View Code on GitHub](https://github.com/applescan/Mi-Casa)

---

## 🌟 Key Features

- 🏡 **Explore My Virtual Home** – Walk through a cozy top-down version of my house and discover interactive hotspots in every room.
- 💬 **Playful Dialogue & Details** – Trigger conversations and object descriptions that reveal little bits of personality throughout the space.
- 🎮 **Eight Mini-Games to Discover** – The house is packed with quick challenges that turn exploration into something more playful and replayable.
- 🏆 **Leaderboards & High Scores** – Compete for top scores in each mini-game with saved leaderboard entries and replay-friendly scoring.
- 📱 **Smooth Desktop + Mobile Play** – Built to work across keyboard, mouse, and touch, with responsive camera behaviour and mobile-friendly mini-game support.

---

## 🕹 Mini-Game Lineup

- 🐟 **Fish Tank** – Rock-paper-scissors
- 🛁 **Bath** – Bubble pop
- 🍿 **Pantry Snacks** – Roach catch
- 🛋 **Sofa** – Remote hunt
- 👕 **Wardrobe** – Laundry sort
- 🐾 **Pet Corner** – Dust bunny chase
- 🍳 **Stove** – Recipe rush
- 🌱 **Succulent** – Water the plants

---

## ✨ Bonus Touches

- 🎥 **Responsive camera movement** that keeps exploration feeling smooth and immersive
- 🔄 **Seamless scene transitions** between the house and mini-games without losing the playful flow
- ☁️ **Database-backed leaderboards** powered by Neon/Postgres, with local fallback storage when needed

---

## 🛠 Built With

- React
- Kaboom.js
- TypeScript
- Vite
- Node.js
- Express
- Neon Postgres
- HTML5 Canvas API
- Vercel Serverless Functions

---

title: Mixtape-me | Spotify App Integration
description: A Spotify app that turns your five most-played tracks into a downloadable, 90s-style mixtape.

body.raw:
![Mixtape cover preview](/img/mixtape/demo1.jpg)
![User mixtape UI](/img/mixtape/demo2.jpg)

> 🎶 Mixtape-me takes your Spotify listening data and turns it into a 90s-style mixtape. It was inspired by CD shops, handmade playlists, and the joy of showing someone what you've been listening to.

---

## 🚀 Try It Out

- 🎧 [Try the App](https://mixtape-me.vercel.app/)
- 💻 [View Code on GitHub](https://github.com/applescan/Mixtape-me)

---

## 🔐 Requirements

Mixtape-me uses the Spotify Web API. To generate your mixtape:

- You must **log in with Spotify** and authorize the app
- Mixtape-me does **not store** or collect any user data
- It fetches your top 5 most-played tracks and visualizes them — that's it!

---

## 🛠 Built With

- HTML / CSS / JavaScript
- Bootstrap
- Spotify Web API
- Heroku
- GitHub
- Figma
- Visual Studio Code

---

## 🗺️ User Guide

- Log in with your Spotify account
- Choose between top songs from:
  - The past month
  - Last 6 months
  - The past year
- View and download your custom mixtape as an image
- Share it with your friends!

---

## 🧠 How It Works

Mixtape-me taps into **Spotify’s Web API** to access your listening history. Once authorized:

- It pulls your top 5 most-played tracks
- Creates a **retro mixtape-style UI** using your song titles, artist names, and cover art
- You can then **download the mixtape image** or take a screenshot for sharing

---

## 🧪 Troubleshooting

**Q: The image won’t download.**
A: Try a different browser or take a screenshot instead.

**Q: The app isn’t working.**
A: Clear cookies or site data for `mixtape-me.herokuapp.com`, or try again on a new device.

---

## 📚 Spotify Developer Dashboard

The project is powered by **Spotify’s official Web API**. Here’s what I did:

- Registered my app on the Spotify Developer Console
- Explored available endpoints for tracks, users, and listening history
- Fetched data in **JSON format** following RESTful principles
- Used that data to design and render mixtape layouts in the app

---

![Spotify stats dashboard](/img/mixtape/stats.jpg)

---

## 📊 Launch Results

People enjoyed making and sharing their playlists in the early days of the project.

> 🎯 My personal goal: **100 mixtapes shared** — and counting!
> User feedback helped refine the UI and highlight unexpected use cases.

---

## 📎 App Access

> Try it here → [https://mixtape-me.vercel.app/](https://mixtape-me.vercel.app/)

title: NZ Veterinary Locum Network
description: A web platform for New Zealand veterinary locums and clinics to find each other without relying on Facebook groups or recruiters.

body.raw:
![Desktop UI](/img/locum/nz-locum1.jpg)
![Mobile Mockup](/img/locum/nz-locum2.jpg)

> The **NZ Veterinary Locum Network** started with a straightforward problem: locums had few places to show their availability, and clinics had no central place to find them. It gives both sides a direct way to connect.

---

## 🖥 Try It Out

- 👉 [Visit the App](https://nz-locum-network.netlify.app/)

---

## 💡 Why Is This Project Important?

There was **no platform** tailored for veterinary locums in NZ to promote themselves outside of recruitment agencies.
New locums who lack clinic connections find it nearly impossible to discover job opportunities.

The **only option** before was a cluttered Facebook group.
This app offers a searchable place for clinics to find and message locums directly.

---

## 🎯 Project Goals

- Create a **central hub** for veterinary job listings and locum profiles
- Help **clinics and doctors connect** without third-party involvement
- Replace the reliance on Facebook groups with a **professional platform**

---

## 🛠 Built With

- Axios
- Bcryptjs
- Express.js
- MongoDB + MongoDB Atlas
- Multer
- Node.js
- Swagger UI
- MDB Bootstrap
- MUI
- React
- Bootstrap / CSS
- Canva + Figma

---

## 👩‍⚕️ User Guide (Doctor)

- Register an account as a **doctor**
- Sign in using your credentials
- You'll be redirected to your profile upon login
- You can:
  - Edit or delete your profile
  - Browse **clinics, jobs, and other doctors**

---

## 🏥 User Guide (Clinic)

- Register an account as a **clinic**
- Sign in using your credentials
- You'll be redirected to your profile upon login
- You can:
  - Edit or delete your clinic profile
  - Add, edit, or delete **job listings**
  - Browse **other clinics, doctors, and jobs**

---

## 🐛 Known Limitation

> ❗ If you upload an image over **1MB**, it may fail due to outdated TLS policies on the cloud server.
> Modern browsers block these uploads due to CORS errors.

You can read more about it [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/create-tls-listener.html).

> ✅ If you run the backend **locally**, this issue should not occur.

---

## 🔮 Future Enhancement

I plan to add **automatic expiration for job listings**.
Once the due date has passed, listings will be hidden or deleted automatically — helping keep the platform clean and up to date.

title: Sarana Dashboard & Point of Sales System
description: A bilingual POS and dashboard I built for my family's shop in Indonesia to manage sales, stock, and orders.

body.raw:
![Sarana dashboard overview](/img/sarana/1.jpg)
![Point of Sales screen](/img/sarana/2.jpg)

> Sarana is the POS and dashboard I built for my family's shop. It helps with the everyday jobs: sales, stock, and orders, in Indonesian or English.

---

## 🚀 Try the App

- 👉 [Visit the App](https://sarana-dashboard.vercel.app/)
- 💻 [View Code on GitHub](https://github.com/applescan/Sarana-Dashboard)

---

## 🧠 Why This Project?

The previous POS setup was slow and cluttered. I made Sarana around the tasks my parents actually need, without adding a pile of features they don't.

---

## 🪄 Unique Touches

- 🇮🇩 **Bilingual Interface** (Indonesian & English)
- 🎯 Custom features tuned to my family's actual workflows
- 🔄 Simplified experience that doesn't overwhelm

---

## 🔐 Key Features

### 📊 Dashboard

- **Real-Time Insights**: Monitor sales, stock, and revenue instantly 🔍
- **AI-Powered Trends**: Built-in OpenAI support for smarter decisions 🤖

### 📦 Product Management

- Powerful **search & filter** tools 🕵️‍♂️
- Instant **stock tracking** 📦
- Easy **admin editing** ✏️

### 📃 Order Management

- Browse by date or keyword 📅
- Modify orders without friction 🧑‍💼
- **Mark as Received** to auto-update stock ✅

---

## ✨ Bonus!

This version uses a test database — so if you see a 404, it's likely the free Supabase tier limit was reached 😅
Still, feel free to explore and let me know what you think!

---

## 🛠 Built With

- Next.js
- Prisma
- Clerk (Auth)
- Tailwind CSS + ShadCN
- GraphQL + Apollo
- OpenAI (AI Insights)
- Supabase (DB)
- Echarts
- TypeScript
- Canva / Figma

---

## 🎥 App Demo

title: [Google Play Japan] Diamond Ship - Tokyo Game Show 2025
description: A browser arcade shooter for Google Play Japan, made to extend Tokyo Game Show 2025 beyond the booth.

body.raw:
![Diamond Ship campaign overview across desktop screens](/img/tgs-2025/image-1.webp)
![Diamond Ship mobile gameplay and leaderboard interface](/img/tgs-2025/image-2.webp)

> For Tokyo Game Show 2025, Google Play Japan took Diamond Ship online: a quick arcade game designed to carry some of the booth's energy beyond the show floor.

---

## Campaign Overview

Diamond Ship turned the Tokyo Game Show activation into a browser-based shooter with seven game worlds inspired by featured IP, hidden boss battles, public and secret leaderboards, and prizes that rewarded repeat play.

It was built as an online extension of the Google Play Japan booth, with enough hidden things and leaderboard competition to make repeat plays worthwhile.

---

## Results

- 74,700 unique visitors
- 242,000 total plays
- 7 minutes and 16 seconds average engagement time
- 257,000 click-throughs to the Google Play Store

---

## Experience Highlights

- Seven bespoke maps designed around different game universes
- Retro-futurist visuals and motion pixel art that matched the event identity
- Hidden stages and boss encounters that added surprise and replay value
- Competitive progression through public and secret leaderboards
- Prize mechanics that connected gameplay with Google Play rewards and merch

---

## My Role

I led the frontend website build from start to finish. I built the public-facing UI, connected the game flows, and worked through the responsive details across desktop and mobile.

I also handled much of the animation work, translating the retro-futurist direction into movement across the interface—from page interactions to smaller presentation details.

---

## Process

### Visual Direction

The art direction balanced nostalgia with a more futuristic arcade feel, transforming static IP assets into a cohesive game universe that felt aligned with the physical TGS installation.

### Animation and World Building

Additional animation across maps, stages, bosses, and interface moments helped the online experience feel lively and immersive, even for players joining remotely.

### Technical Foundation

The game was built from scratch with Phaser 4 and Matter.js, supported by a custom Tiled map editor workflow used to refine level layouts, attack patterns, and difficulty tuning.

### Playtesting and Balancing

Enemy behavior, boss attack angles, and gameplay pacing were iterated throughout development to keep the challenge sharp without losing approachability.

---

## Built With

- Angular
- TypeScript
- HTML5 + CSS3
- Node.js
- Phaser 4
- Matter.js physics
- Custom Tiled map editor integration
- Browser-based game architecture
- Motion pixel art and interface animation

---

title: [Google Play] Diamond Castle – Tokyo Game Show 2024
description: A vertical mini-game and event site for Google Play Japan at Tokyo Game Show 2024, made for people at the show and at home.

body.raw:
![Diamond Castle Gameplay](/img/tgs/tgs-1.webp)
![Retro-inspired UI Design](/img/tgs/tgs-2.webp)

> **Diamond Castle** is a vertical speed runner made with Google Play Japan for Tokyo Game Show 2024. It brought a little of the event online in a mobile-friendly game with a retro look.

---

## 🎥 Campaign Showreel

- 💻 [View Reel on Youtube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w1Huo7F7S4I&list=TLGGfN2m5Wtxa9swOTA3MjAyNQ)

---

## 🌟 Key Highlights

- 🏰 **Original Mini-Game** – A vertical climber game with smooth mobile controls and high replay value.
- 📱 **Online + On-Site** – Built to extend the Tokyo Game Show experience beyond the exhibit hall.
- 🎁 **Reward System** – Leaderboard ranks, social sharing, and early sign-ups unlocked exclusive giveaways.
- 🤝 **Cross-Studio Collaboration** – Designed in partnership with Kayac and Hakuhodo for Google Play Japan.
- 🎮 **Game Dev Collabs** – Integrated content from top developers like HoYoverse and Bandai Namco.

---

## 🛠 My Role

As a frontend developer on the team, I worked on the website interface, homepage layout, and mobile performance. I also worked closely with designers to carry the retro visual direction through the site.

---

## 🔧 The Process

- 🧭 **User Flow & Wireframing** – Established clear content structure and intuitive player journey from landing to game.
- 🧱 **Asset Refinement** – Ensured pixel-perfect placement of characters, objects, and collision zones.
- 🎨 **Visual Balance** – Merged Google Play’s bold identity with Diamond Castle’s playful, nostalgic style.
- 🧩 **Iterative Collaboration** – Worked side-by-side with Japanese designers and developers to align gameplay feel with real-world event excitement.

---

## 🧠 Designed For

- Tokyo Game Show 2024
- VIP Event Attendees
- Casual mobile gamers
- Game community on social platforms (X, LINE, etc.)

---

## 🛠 Built With

- Angular
- TypeScript
- Pixi.js
- CSS3 + HTML5
- Node.js
- Game analytics tools

---

## 🎥 Campaign Showreel

<video controls width="100%" preload="auto">
  <source src="/img/tgs/carousel1.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>
<video controls width="100%" preload="auto">
  <source src="/img/tgs/carousel2.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>

---

> Diamond Castle brought the energy of Tokyo Game Show to life online — letting players everywhere climb, compete, and celebrate the joy of gaming. 🎮✨

title: What to Eat - A Recipe Recommendation Engine 🌭🥫
description: A recipe finder that suggests meals from the ingredients you have and your dietary preferences.

body.raw:
![Recipe Generator UI](/img/what-to-eat/What-to-eat-1.png)
![Mockup Screen](/img/what-to-eat/What-to-eat-2.png)

> What to Eat is for the familiar “what can I make with this?” moment. Add the ingredients you have and any dietary preferences, and it suggests recipes instead of letting food sit forgotten in the fridge.

---

## 🍴 Try the App

- 👉 [Visit the App](https://what-to-eat-2.vercel.app/)
- 💻 [View Code on GitHub](https://github.com/applescan/what-to-eat-2)
- 🚀 [Featured on Product Hunt](https://www.producthunt.com/products/what-to-eat-2)

---

## 💡 Why This Project?

This started as a fun side project to explore **TypeScript** and **Next.js**.
It’s grown into a tool I actually use when I don’t know what to cook. 🤓

---

## 🎯 Goals

- ✅ Help users **reduce food waste**
- ✅ Make meal planning easier
- ✅ Inspire people to **cook more at home**
- ✅ Empower users with dietary restrictions

---

## 🧑‍🍳 How to Use

1. Click **"Get Recipe"** on the homepage
2. Choose your dietary preferences
3. Enter ingredients you have
4. Hit **Next** to get personalized recipe ideas
5. Click on a recipe to view details

---

## 🐛 Known Limitations

- Typos in ingredients may cause search failures — user input must be precise
- Occasionally, the Spoonacular API may return ingredients outside selected dietary filters

---

## 🚀 Future Enhancements

- Integrate **NLP** to auto-correct input typos in the ingredient form
- Add **meal planning** features
- Let users **save favorite recipes** for future access

---

## 🛠 Built With

- T3 Stack
- React
- TypeScript
- Next.js
- Prisma
- Tailwind CSS
- tRPC
- NextAuth.js
- Spoonacular API
- Canva / Figma

---

## 📱 Live App

> Explore recipe at
> 👉 [https://what-to-eat-2.vercel.app/](https://what-to-eat-2.vercel.app/)

title: Whazup — NZ Event Discovery App
description: A swipe-based way to find New Zealand events using the Eventfinda API.

body.raw:
![Whazup UI 1](/img/whazup/whazup.png)
![Whazup UI 2](/img/whazup/whazup-2.png)

> Whazup helps you find things to do around New Zealand without digging through long event lists. Answer a few swipe-based questions and it uses your interests to surface concerts, workshops, festivals, and more.

---

## 👉 Try Whazup

- 👉 **Live app:** https://Whazup.vercel.app/
- 💻 **Source code:** https://github.com/applescan/Whazup

---

## 💡 Why this project?

I made Whazup to see whether a quick, mobile-first onboarding flow could make local event discovery feel less like admin. It uses Tinder-style swipes to learn what you're into, then pulls matching events and locations from Eventfinda.

---

## 🎯 Goals

-  Provide **personalised event recommendations** based on user interests
-  Offer **localised event discovery** across New Zealand
-  Deliver **fast, mobile-first UI/UX** with a swipe-style questionnaire
-  Cover diverse event categories (music, theatre, sports, festivals, workshops)

---

## 🧭 User Flow

1. Welcome — choose a region or allow automatic location suggestions.
2. Swipe interface — go through curated questions to indicate your tastes.
3. Matching — the app analyses preferences and matches event categories.
4. Results — celebratory match + curated events list.
5. Event details — book through Eventfinda links when available.

---

## 📚 Event Categories

Whazup covers eight major categories:
1. Concerts & Gig Guide
2. Performing Arts
3. Theatre
4. Sports & Outdoors
5. Festivals & Lifestyle
6. Dance
7. Exhibitions
8. Workshops & Classes.

---

## 🛠 Built With

- **Next.js 14** (App Router)
- **TypeScript**
- **Tailwind CSS**
- **Framer Motion** (animations & gestures)
- **Lucide React** (icons)
- **Eventfinda API** (events & locations)
- Next.js API Routes, SSR, image optimisation & caching.

---

## 🚀 Features

- Tinder-style swipe questionnaire for interest matching.
- 180+ questions created across the app (curated set for onboarding).
- Location-based filtering & region grouping across New Zealand.
- Glassmorphism UI, animated backgrounds, responsive layout, and PWA-friendly touches.
